title: Optimist or Pessimist? The Inevitable Triumph of Truth
summary: 'Remember that all through history the way of truth and love has always won. There have been tyrants and murderers, and for a time they seem invincible, but in the end, they always fall.'
keywords: Optimist or Pessimist? The Inevitable Triumph of Truth
full_text:
In 1944, World War II had reached its murderous crescendo. Millions lay dead across European and Asian battlefields, Nazi concentration camps were operating at full fury, and the shadow of the atomic bomb loomed on the horizon.

Released from detention at the Aga Khan Palace, Gandhi was visited by an exhausted war correspondent.

The journalist asked with deep melancholy:
"Mr. Gandhi! The entire world is drowning in blood, tanks, and aerial bombs. Despots rule vast continents. In this nightmare of brutality, do you honestly believe that non-violence has any future?
Tell me: are you an incurable optimist, or have you finally surrendered to pessimism?"

Gandhi looked at the journalist with eyes of unfathomable calm. His voice possessed the certainty of eternal rock:

"My friend! I am an incurable optimist!
Do you know why?
When I despair, I remember that all through history the way of truth and love has always won!
There have been tyrants and murderers, and for a time they seem invincible. Think of Genghis Khan, think of Nero, think of the despots of every age!
For a season, they march across the earth, crushing everything beneath their iron heels.
**But in the end, they always fall! Think of it: ALWAYS!**

No darkness has ever existed that could extinguish the light of a single candle.
Brute force is temporary; truth and compassion are eternal.
I shall live and die in the unshakable certainty that love is mightier than the sword!"

The journalist was moved to tears.

Within three years, the mighty British Empire departed Indian shores without a war, and the despots of Europe lay in ruins—vindicating Gandhi's eternal prophecy.
moral: Despair is a choice; history proves that tyranny is transient and the moral arc of the universe bends toward justice.
